source_refs.note: 5- Inhalants: a main subheading of 15.7.2 Use and Abuse of Drugs, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 49-49.

blocks.text: Inhalants, such as nail polish remover and glue, are psychoactive substances that are inhaled to produce senses of euphoria, relaxation, and altered perception. They can produce a range of negative health effects, such as respiratory problems, cognitive impairment, and neurological damage.

The withdrawal symptoms of drug abuse include anxiety, depression, fatigue, agitation, mood swings, shakiness or tremors, headache, sweating, nausea, loss of appetite, insomnia, rapid heart rate, high blood pressure, hallucinations (visual, auditory, or tactile), and seizures.
